D. H. Lawrence, Lady Chatterley’s Lover.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/d-h-lawrence/lady-chatterleys-lover

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- D. H. Lawrence, the author, died 1930 (Wikidata Q34970, P570 = 1930-03-02).

First publication of the text used: 1929 (SE colophon: 'Lady Chatterley’s Lover was published in 1929 by D. H. Lawrence.'). The Wikipedia article on the novel says it was first published privately in 1928 in Florence, Italy, and in 1929 in Paris, France. Both places give the same result below.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the edition's own statement of rights (quoted below) says the text is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (Italy, first publication 1928 in Florence): copyright lasts for life plus 70 years after the death of the last person named above. The author died in 1930, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 2001. If the origin were France (Paris, 1929), the result is the same: the author died in 1930, before 1937, so the French wartime extension does not apply.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: published 1929 by D. H. Lawrence
- Wikidata Q34970 (D. H. Lawrence), P570 = 1930-03-02
